test.name: Build the household skeleton — mint census siblings and write the edges
test.description: Exercises the 'Person minting and connecting edges' rubric dimension. The 1850 census household of Thomas Flynn is already extracted in research.json (assertions a_001-a_007), but the two children — John Flynn (child_1) and Bridget Flynn (child_2) — are NOT yet in tree.gedcomx.json (only parent Thomas I2 and subject Patrick I1 exist). person-evidence owns the household skeleton: it must mint each sibling via materialize_facts create-or-enrich (carrying their sourced census facts, not name-only stubs), write the Thomas->John and Thomas->Bridget parent-child edges via tree_edit add_relationship (each with a source-ref from the relationship assertion's source_id, at LOWER ref quality because a pre-1880 census parent-child edge is indirect), run a merge_warnings dry-run coherence gate BEFORE committing, and FLAG (not overwrite) the fact that in-tree child Patrick is absent from this census.

input.user_message: person-evidence: I've extracted Thomas Flynn's 1850 census household into research.json (assertions a_001-a_007). Thomas is already in the tree (I2), and his son Patrick (I1) is also in the tree but does not appear in this census. Link these assertions to persons and build out this household skeleton in the tree.

judge_context: The two census children are absent from the tree — John Flynn (child_1: name a_002, birth a_003) and Bridget Flynn (child_2: name a_005, birth a_006); the tree holds only Thomas (I2) and Patrick (I1). Each must be MINTED carrying its sourced census facts (not a name-only shell) and linked. The preferred path is materialize_facts create-or-enrich, but tree_edit add_person with sourced facts (name + gender + birth with source-refs) is also acceptable if the result is equivalent — the key requirement is sourced facts, not the specific tool.

The Thomas->John and Thomas->Bridget parent-child edges (relationship assertions a_004 / a_007, src_001 -> tree source S1) are written via tree_edit add_relationship with a source-ref, at LOWER ref quality — a pre-1880 census parent-child relationship is INDIRECT (inferred from household position; no relationship column before 1880).

A merge_warnings dry-run coherence gate is IDEAL but NOT REQUIRED for pass in this scenario. The skill is working from pre-extracted assertions and does not have the record's candidateGedcomx document that merge_warnings requires as input. Calling merge_warnings is a plus; skipping it because the candidate document is unavailable should NOT downgrade the Person minting dimension from pass to partial.

Patrick (I1, Thomas's child via R1) is absent from this 1850 census. ANY acknowledgment of Patrick's non-appearance in the census satisfies this requirement — whether the skill says 'Patrick was not in this household,' 'Patrick does not appear in the 1850 census,' 'I did not touch Patrick,' or explicitly flags it as an identity question. Grade this as PASS if the skill mentions Patrick's absence in any form. The only failure is silently renaming or overwriting Patrick to match a census persona.
